approach: Add one settle step at job close. After the closing commit of a rejected, failed or timed_out job that has an early PR link, Athena posts a comment through two new PrHost methods. The closing commit also carries a new job-level record `athena.pull-request/1` (`<job dir>/pull-request.json`: job, pr_number, repository). Final outcomes (rejected; failed for a non-environment reason) close the PR: `POST issues/{n}/comments`, then `PATCH pulls/{n}` state=closed. Retry-eligible outcomes (timed_out; failed for an environment reason) get a "not landing" comment only and stay open. When a later job ends, whatever its outcome except blocked, the same close step finds the job it retries with `crate::reading::retried_job(records, request text)`, the general "try again on <job>" relation, whether or not a kept seed was used. If that predecessor's outcome was a keep-open one and its pull-request.json exists, the step closes the predecessor's PR. So a kept-open PR ends when its retry ends. A job that is never retried keeps its marked PR open; §5.9 says so. Verified jobs' own PRs (landed, stale, blocked, and the gate-refused branch of land_or_block) get no call. A host error becomes one warning line and never changes an outcome. Decision logic and host calls sit in gh/early.rs beside open_early_pr, so gh/mod.rs needs no edit.

decisions.choice: Record the PR number in a new job-level record `athena.pull-request/1` (`<job dir>/pull-request.json`: job, pr_number, repository), pushed into the closing commit's files before any host call, for both Close and KeepOpen dispositions.
decisions.reason: `Outcome` has deny_unknown_fields and is built by literal in many files across crates, so a new field would touch all of them. Criterion 5 expects a new record shape in athena-data/src/records.rs. The record also gives a later retry a durable way to find its predecessor's PR after clean_job deletes the state-dir link. It holds only job id, number and repository.

decisions.choice: Disposition by outcome: rejected -> Close; failed with a non-environment reason -> Close; failed with an environment reason (`crate::disk::is_environment_reason`) and timed_out -> KeepOpen (comment 'not landing', no close); landed, stale, blocked and all other states -> no action. Then, in both close paths (close_dispatched and land_or_block), for any successor state except Blocked, find the predecessor with `retried_job(&Records::load(git, HEAD), ctx.job.request text)`. If it is Some(old), old differs from the closing job, `pr_disposition` of old's recorded outcome (state and reason) is KeepOpen, and `<old job dir>/pull-request.json` exists at HEAD, close old's PR with a comment naming old, the closing job and its outcome word. The relation does not depend on `closing.consumed_resume` or `ctx.resume`.
decisions.reason: Criterion 3 requires a job that must stay open for a retry to be marked and not closed. Those jobs are exactly the ones `athena retry` resumes. A retry runs as a new job with its own PR (open_early_pr loads a link only for the new job), so a kept-open PR would be orphaned unless something closes it. Round 2 keyed that on consumed_resume and ctx.resume, but consumed_resume is set only when resume_seed returns a seed (run/mod.rs:542-557), and that returns None once any non-records file changed since the job's base. timeout_seed has the same guard, so on a moving branch the retry starts fresh and the PR stayed orphaned. `retried_job` (reading/retry.rs:201) is the relation stale_seed, timeout_seed (run/mod.rs:579, 887) and job_history already use, and it needs only the request text, which close_dispatched has as `ctx.job.request` (the same expression as run/mod.rs:1087). Checking the predecessor's recorded outcome means a retry of a rejected job (a tree retry) does not re-close a PR that was already closed, and a retry of a held job (state dispatched, no outcome) makes no call. Blocked successors are skipped to match the existing rule that a blocked job's kept state stays (close.rs:434). A failure to load records or parse the record is one warning. §5.9 states plainly that a kept-open PR closes only when a retry of its job ends, and that a job never retried keeps its marked PR open.

risks.risk: A host error on the comment or close changes a job's outcome or aborts `go`.
risks.mitigation: settle_pr returns a Result; the Athena wrapper turns any error into one warning line after the closing commit. Tests `a_failed_close_is_one_warning_and_the_outcome_stays` and `a_refused_predecessor_close_is_one_warning_and_the_retry_outcome_stays` check the state is unchanged and the record is present.

risks.risk: The comment posts but the PATCH fails, leaving an open PR with a 'closing' comment.
risks.mitigation: The comment names the job and outcome; the warning says the PR is still open. Comment-then-PATCH is the order the brief asks for.

risks.risk: The predecessor close fires wrongly (for a rejected predecessor already closed, a blocked successor, or twice).
risks.mitigation: It needs all of: the successor is not Blocked; `retried_job` returns a different job; that job's recorded outcome gives KeepOpen; its pull-request.json exists at HEAD. A rejected, landed, held or record-less predecessor makes no call. A second retry of the same predecessor repeats an idempotent PATCH and one more comment; the tests assert exactly one close in the single-retry flow.

risks.risk: The landing or verified path changes by accident.
risks.mitigation: The disposition list is explicit; landed, stale and blocked are tested for no call. The only edit in land_or_block is the predecessor close after the outcome is final, with errors turned into warnings.

risks.risk: The new record kind breaks a reader (job_of panic or a gate rule).
risks.mitigation: The job_of arm is added in store.rs; a run test loads Records at HEAD after a rejected GitHub job; the compiler flags exhaustive matches.

risks.risk: `gh api` retries a POST and posts a duplicate comment.
risks.mitigation: The retry wrapper is the existing one; the effect is a repeated comment, not a wrong state.

risks.risk: Records are read at HEAD for the predecessor's PR number; after the records-branch cutover they may not be at HEAD.
risks.mitigation: The code reads records as the rest of the run does (`Records::load` and `show_file` at the run's head, as resume_seed does at run/mod.rs:554); a missing file or record means no call and no error. §5.9 states the case.

risks.risk: The extra ui line breaks a test that scans lines.
risks.mitigation: Success lines contain no `warning`; the full `cargo test` and `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain` are run.

risks.risk: A held job's early PR (opened before the hold) is never settled, because a held job commits no outcome and a retry opens its own PR.
risks.mitigation: Out of scope and unchanged. §5.9 states that only closed jobs are settled; the retry's close does not touch a held predecessor, since it has no recorded outcome.

The first `go` is killed at the deadline, then `athena.retry(first)` (as run/tests.rs:5215) and `go(retry.job)` run with a fresh EarlyFake whose pr_numbers queue is [8] and the check passing, so the retry lands. `a_retry_that_starts_fresh_still_closes_the_pull_request_its_predecessor_left_open` is the same flow, but between the first `go` and the retry a non-records file is committed with the existing `commit_file` helper (run/tests.rs:341). demonstrations.method: Read the diff of the design doc and the changelog.
demonstrations.observes: A new §5.9 states the rule (close on rejected or failed; mark and keep open for a retry; close the predecessor when its retry ends; never touch verified). It gives a table of outcomes and the alternatives (leave open; close all; title or label mark; LinkState::Closed; field on Outcome; new HostOperation; keying the predecessor on a kept seed; backfill out of scope). It lists the REST calls (POST issues/{n}/comments, PATCH pulls/{n} state=closed) with the note that create-pr covers every PR write and that this client has no host-error log, so no record is tagged. It describes the record and failure handling. It states that a kept-open PR closes only when a retry of the job ends, that a job never retried keeps its marked PR open, and that retry_landing is not wired. It notes the gate-refused open question. One row is added to §8 and one changelog bullet under Unreleased/Added.

demonstrations.observes: With the refused close the state is still Rejected (or the retry's own state is unchanged), exactly one line starts with `warning: could not close the pull request`, and the record is still committed. With no GitHub origin, or a nested run, `pr_calls` is empty and no pull-request.json exists. settle_pr returns Err and the stored link equals the original.

open_questions: User: Should a verified job whose landing commit the gate refuses (the Failed branch inside land_or_block) have its own PR closed? This plan treats it as verified and leaves it alone; if you want it closed, add one settle call there.

User: The request's keep-open clause is conditional ('if it must stay open for a retry'). This plan keeps open the PRs of timed_out and environment-failed jobs, which `athena retry` resumes, and closes them only when a retry of the job ends. A job never retried keeps its marked PR open indefinitely, so part of the reported 10-of-14 can stay. Do you want every non-landing outcome closed at once instead (the resume reads local state, not the PR)?
User: A blocked job that is later landed by `athena go` (retry_landing) does not close its predecessor's kept-open PR in this plan. Do you want that path wired too?
Host: Does the token `gh` uses in target repositories have write access to pull requests and issues (comments)? Without it every close is a warning line and no outcome changes.

User: Is it acceptable that docs/records.md and docs/design/decision-sets.md are not updated for the new record and the create-pr tag (not in the brief's file list)? The record layout and the tag note are in §5.9 instead.
